Global Head of Project Procurement & Process Excellence
  
  
and is part of Global Sourcing organisation, located in Singapore and will be an
  
  
on-site role
  
  
.
  
  
**In this role, you will have the opportunity to:**  
Lead project procurement and sourcing readiness for assigned NPI and other strategic projects from early development through industrialization and handover, including procurement scope, sourcing plans, milestones, resource needs, budgets, supplier selection, qualification and readiness, prototype and pre-series sourcing, material availability, project risks and recovery actions.
  
  
Drive early supplier involvement, cost optimization and commercial activities by partnering with R&D, Quality, Industrial Engineering, Commodity Management and other stakeholders on design reviews, Design-to-Cost, standardization, modularization and make-or-buy assessments; analyzing cost drivers and Total Cost of Ownership; and negotiating project-related commercial terms and development agreements in alignment with applicable approval processes.
  
  
Design, implement and continuously improve procurement processes across Global Sourcing, including end-to-end processes, procedures, templates, roles and controls; drive standardization and harmonization across regions, sites and teams; maintain assigned procurement playbook content; and support process ownership, governance, version control and training.
  
  
Advance procurement process excellence, performance and digitalization by applying DBS and structured problem-solving methods to identify root causes, eliminate waste and reduce manual effort; identify automation and digitalization opportunities; translate business needs into requirements for procurement systems and tools; and define and track process KPIs, adoption metrics and improvement actions.
  
  
Strengthen procurement compliance, governance and risk management by maintaining procurement-specific governance frameworks, procedures, controls and evidence requirements; performing process compliance reviews and risk assessments; coordinating corrective and preventive actions; supporting supplier due diligence, onboarding and third-party risk management; and representing Global Sourcing in relevant internal and external audits.

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, or a related field.

Demonstrated experience supporting NPI or product-development projects, including supplier selection, prototype sourcing, industrialization readiness, cost management, and project risk mitigation.
  
  
Proven experience in procurement process improvement, including process mapping, standardization, continuous improvement, governance, and implementation of sustainable changes.
  
  
Experience in commercial and contract negotiations and working knowledge of procurement systems and digital tools such as SAP, e-procurement platforms, Microsoft Office, Power BI, workflow tools, and process-mapping applications.

Willingness to travel internationally, estimated up to 20%.

·
  
  
Project management or continuous-improvement certification, such as PMP, Lean, or Six Sigma.
  
  
High-mix, low-volume, medical device, life science, or precision-instrument environments.
  
  
Process-management or audit/compliance training.

title: Head of Talent Acquisition, APAC
description:
**Description**

Meltwater is seeking a strategic and hands-on Head of Talent Acquisition, APAC to lead talent acquisition across the Asia-Pacific region. This leader will partner closely with regional business and People leaders to build strong talent strategies, improve hiring quality and speed, strengthen recruiting capability, and ensure a consistent, inclusive candidate experience across APAC markets.

The successful candidate will balance strategic leadership with practical execution. They will use data, market insight, technology, and strong stakeholder partnerships to help Meltwater attract, assess, and hire exceptional talent while building a high-performing regional Talent Acquisition function.

**What You’ll Do**

* Own APAC Talent Acquisition strategy including end-to-end sourcing and recruiting across all functions, with a heavy emphasis on GTM hiring with the ability to support broader regional workforce priorities
* Partner with APAC leadership, people leaders and hiring managers to understand workforce plans, define critical hiring priorities and create practical recruiting strategies
* Lead, coach, and develop the APAC Talent Acquisition team clarifying goals, strengthening capability, and creating a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
* Establish consistent, high-quality recruiting practices while adapting appropriately to local market requirements and candidate expectations
* Improve hiring outcomes through structured intake, calibrated assessment, effective interview practices, and clear decision-making and ownership across the hiring process
* Build trusted relationships with senior stakeholders and provide market insight, talent data, and recommendations that support sound workforce decisions
* Strengthen sourcing strategies, employer brand, talent pipelines, and regional market presence across the APAC markets
* Partner with People, Legal, HRIS, Total Rewards, and other teams to support compliant and effective hiring practices.
* Use recruiting data and technology to identify trends, improve processes, and increase efficiency and strengthen the candidate and hiring manager experience
* Support Meltwater’s evolving approach to AI in Talent Acquisition, including responsible adoption and safeguards against fraudulent or misrepresented candidate activity.
* Promote inclusive hiring practices and ensure recruitment decisions are fair, consistent and grounded in job-related evidence
* Contribute to global Talent Acquisition programs and represent APAC perspectives in global initiatives.

**How You’ll Work with AI**

At Meltwater, we believe AI fluency, curiosity, and responsible experimentation are increasingly important to how we work and create value for our customers. In this role, you will be encouraged to understand how AI can improve your work, enhance decision-making, increase efficiency, and help us build better experiences and solutions. You do not need to be an AI expert, but you should be curious, open to learning, and thoughtful about using AI responsibly.

As a Talent Acquisition leader, you will help the team build practical AI fluency, identify meaningful opportunities to use AI-enabled tools, and establish safeguards that protect candidate fairness, privacy, authenticity, and human judgment. This includes supporting responsible adoption of AI in sourcing, market analysis, recruiting operations, interview preparation, and reporting, while helping the organization detect and address fraudulent or misrepresented candidate activity. AI should support, not replace, human accountability, candidate relationships, collaboration, and hiring decisions

**What You’ll Bring**

**Required Qualifications**

* Experience leading Talent Acquisition across multiple APAC markets, especially India, China, Australia and Japan
* Strong understanding of APAC talent markets, employment laws, and market considerations.
* Proven experience leading, coaching and developing recruiters across a range of experience levels
* Strong business partnership skills with the ability to influence senior leaders and hiring managers and translate business priorities into hiring strategies
* Experience building, improving and glocalizing regional recruiting strategies, operating models and processes.

title: Receptionist
description:
**Job Description**

CBRE is the global leader in commercial real estate services and investments. With services, insights and data that span every dimension of the industry, we create solutions for clients of every size, in every sector and across every geography. CBRE is the place where talented people who want to do impactful work can realize potential in every dimension.

**CBRE Global Workplace Solutions (GWS)**

As one of CBRE's core global businesses, Global Workplace Solutions (GWS) provides end-to-end services to occupier clients across the entire lifecycle of a building.

Our teams help companies improve their operations and reduce costs, through expert facilities management, project management, real estate and energy and sustainability services. Our dedicated teams work across all industries, and support clients ranging from the Fortune 500 global companies to single, iconic buildings.

**About the Role:**

The Receptionist shapes the experience everyone has from the moment they walk through the door. You're the first person most people see when they walk through the door — that greeting, that eye contact, that sense someone is glad they arrived, sets the tone for everything that follows. On a well-run site, it's never an accident. You own the lobby, the visitor process, the conference room calendar, and the daily logistics of a busy front desk. You will be successful in this role when you make every visitor and employee feel expected and well taken care of, and run the front desk reliably enough that no one has to think about it.

**What You'll Do: Front Desk & Visitors**

* Greet clients, applicants, and visitors, issue visitor and parking passes, and apply security protocols so every guest feels expected.
* Receive and direct incoming calls to the appropriate personnel or voicemail so callers reach the right person.

**Meetings & Hospitality**

* Schedule and prepare meeting and conference rooms, including room setup, catering orders, and equipment, so meetings start on time.
* Request building and housekeeping services to maintain the condition of shared spaces.
* Arrange hospitality services for guests, including transportation, tickets, and reservations.

**Mail & Office Coordination**

* Track incoming and outgoing packages, mail, and freight, and arrange messenger service.
* Handle general clerical duties, distribute faxes and packages, and order office supplies so employees have what they need.

**What You Need:**

* Experience in customer service, hospitality, or an office environment
* Strong verbal communication skills and a professional phone manner
* Comfortable with standard workplace and collaboration tools (email, documents, spreadsheets, and scheduling)
* Ability to follow established procedures reliably and consistently
* Strong preference for experience in a corporate, hotel, or premium-service environment, familiarity with visitor-management systems, and coordinating conference rooms or catering

**This Role Is a Good Fit If You:**

* Get energy from imparting kindness, help, and recommendations to others. The more people you interact with in a day, the better you feel when you head home.
* Are known for noticing a guest, friend, or family members needs something before they ask. People constantly tell you "I can't believe you read my mind on that."
* Stay warm and even-keeled under pressure: whether it's the morning rush, an early VIP, or a caller who's already frustrated, and people notice you never seem rattled.
* Look forward to being at the desk before anyone else arrives, so you're the one setting the tone from the first hello.
* Are a stickler for details. You feel at your best when every visitor's information is logged, every conference room reservation is made, every I dotted and T crossed.

**Why CBRE**

When you join CBRE, you become part of the global leader in commercial real estate services and investment that helps businesses and people thrive. We are dynamic problem solvers and forward-thinking professionals who create significant impact. Our collaborative culture is built on our shared values — respect, integrity, service and excellence — and we value the diverse perspectives, backgrounds and skillsets of our people. At CBRE, you have the opportunity to chart your own course and realize your potential. We welcome all applicants.

Applicant AI Use Disclosure

We value human interaction to understand each candidate's unique experience, skills and aspirations. We do not use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to make hiring decisions, and we ask that candidates disclose any use of AI in the application and interview process.

If the above interests you, we would love to hear from you!

 **Additional Information**

If you require any adjustments or support in connection with your application or the recruitment process, please contact Candidate.Care@cbre.com. We are committed to ensuring that all candidates can participate fully in the process.

title: Cluster Network Head – SEA ANZ
description:
#### **About this Position**

The Cluster Network Head of SEA AND is responsible for end-to-end quality management across Henkel’s Seven manufacturing sites in South-East Asia and Australia / New Zealand. This role is to drive and implement a consistent Network quality strategy to enhance customer satisfaction and support achieving financial targets.

**Some of the key objectives include:**

* Compliance with Henkel’s global quality standards
* Fostering a Zero-Defect culture and customer intimacy
* Driving digital transformation to simplify, standardize and efficiency
* Developing people/ competencies / critical talent pipeline and delivering key initiatives aligned with AOQ's PDIs and performance KPI’s

#### **What you'll do**

**Quality Cluster Leadership**

* Lead a team of quality professionals in the sites, develop team members.
* Lead the day-to-day operation of quality processes for a group of manufacturing sites.
* Identify systemic issues across the Network and drive to resolution, escalate critical issues to Regional Quality Head
* Responsible for stopping the processing, shipment, or use of poor-quality products.
* Animate critical customer escalations for the plants in scope providing the customer and internal stakeholders with clarity and pace of problem resolutions with CAPA

**Quality System Deployment**

* Achieve 100% compliance with mandatory minimum CtQ standards by target deadlines.
* Conduct monthly MOC/ADP governance reviews at each site to ensure proactive quality risk control.

**Ensure full implementation and governance of Henkel’s five global quality fundamentals across all SEA and ANZ plants:**

* Statistical Quality Control (SQC)
* Management of Change (MOC)
* Critical to Quality (CtQ) Standards
* Problem Solving Tools (FRPS / A3 / Six Sigma)
* Process Failure Mode & Effects Analysis (PFMEA)

  

#### **What makes you a good fit**

* Master’s degree in engineering (Chemical / Electrical / Mechanical etc)
* 5+ years of Multi-site Quality Management experience in leadership role or a related technical discipline.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing quality management, preferably in chemical, automotive, aerospace or electronics industries.
* Proven track record of deploying global quality systems such as SQC, MOC, PFMEA, and problem-solving tools in multi-site environments.
* Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional and cross-cultural teams in a matrix organization.
* Strong customer-facing skills, with experience managing quality expectations of tier-1 global clients.
* Understanding of Quality Standards and Requirements including ISO / VDA / IATF / PPAP etc…
* Certified in Six Sigma / Lean Management / Auditor Experience / Root Cause Analysis
* Excellent communication skills in English. Proficiency in one or more Southeast Asian languages may be beneficial where required for business interactions with customers, suppliers, or stakeholders in specific markets

#### **Some perks of joining Henkel**

* Flexible work scheme with flexible hours, hybrid work model, and work from anywhere policy for up to 30 days per year
* Diverse national and international growth opportunities
* Global wellbeing standards with health and preventive care programs
* Gender-neutral parental leave for a minimum of 8 weeks
* Employee Share Plan with voluntary investment and Henkel matching shares
* Outpatient Medical and Specialist Coverage for employees and eligible dependents
* Life, Hospital, Personal Accident Insurance Coverage
* Flexible Benefits covering Dental, Vaccination, Eye screenings etc for employees and eligible dep
* Access to company products at discounted price

At Henkel, we come from a broad range of backgrounds, perspectives, and life experiences. We believe the uniqueness of all our employees is the power in us. Become part of the team and bring your uniqueness to us! We welcome all applications across different genders, origins, cultures, religions, sexual orientations, disabilities, and generations.

title: Operations Trainer (Cleaning)
description:
About the Role
  
  
We are seeking an experienced and hands-on Operations Trainer (Cleaning) to support the training and development of frontline employees and supervisors across Hong Ye Group sites.
  
  
The successful candidate will provide practical on-the-job training, coach supervisors and new hires, reinforce operational standards, and work closely with L&OD to ensure that training materials and SOPs remain relevant to actual site practices.
  
  
This is a predominantly field-based role suited to an experienced cleaning professional who is confident in demonstrating cleaning methods, guiding employees and supervisors, and providing practical coaching directly at the workplace.
  
  
Key Responsibilities
  
  
New-Hire OJT and Supervisor Coaching
  
  

* Provide structured on-the-job training for new hires, covering cleaning methods, work sequencing, equipment use, chemical handling, basic safety requirements and site-specific practices.
* Use a practical coaching method of explain, demonstrate, allow practice, observe, correct and recheck to confirm that employees can perform assigned tasks safely and correctly.
* Conduct follow-up coaching after initial OJT to identify gaps and reinforce areas where additional guidance is required.
* Complete the required OJT and coaching records provided by L&OD, and submit documentation to the Head of L&OD within the required timeline.
* Provide hands-on coaching to supervisors who require stronger operational knowledge or greater confidence in guiding frontline employees.
* Observe how supervisors conduct toolbox briefings, coach employees and manage cleaning practices, then provide practical feedback and guidance.
* Act as an experienced mentor and operational reference point for both junior and experienced frontline employees.

Training and SOP Development
  
  

* Work with L&OD to develop and refine practical training materials, SOPs, visual guides, checklists and OJT resources based on actual site requirements.
* Contribute technical and operational expertise so that training materials remain accurate, realistic and suitable for frontline use.
* Conduct or support internal practical training in cleaning methodology, machinery operation, chemical handling, carpet care, washroom cleaning and other relevant cleaning processes.
* Identify recurring knowledge and skill gaps across sites and recommend new, refresher or targeted training interventions.
* Highlight situations where documented procedures require greater clarity, practicality or site-specific adaptation.
* Provide feedback to L&OD on the effectiveness and usability of training resources after they have been applied on-site.
* Support internal training delivery only unless otherwise assigned. External training programmes and vendor coordination remain under the Head of L&OD.

Capability Building
  
  

* Conductscheduled capability visits across sites to observe operational practices andidentify areas requiring coaching or reinforcement.
* Check that required toolbox briefings are conducted and assess whether supervisors deliver them meaningfully, rather than treating them only as an attendance requirement.
* Provide immediate coaching and correction where gaps are observed, instead of limiting the visit to documenting non-compliance.
* Check that required toolbox briefings are conducted and assess whether supervisors deliver them meaningfully, rather than treating them only as an attendance requirement.
* Provide immediate coaching and correction where gaps are observed, instead of limiting the visit to documenting non-compliance.

Requirements
  
  
Mandatory Qualifications
  
  

* Minimum 6 years of relevant experience in commercial cleaning operations, cleaning supervision or a similar hands-on role.
* Strong practical knowledge of cleaning methods, machinery, equipment, chemicals and workplace practices.
* Proven experience in training, coaching or mentoring cleaners and supervisors.
* Able to demonstrate cleaning procedures and provide practical on-the-job guidance at operational sites.
* Willing to travel across multiple work sites and work a combination of morning, night and weekend shifts when required.
* Relevant WSQ cleaning qualifications arepreferred but not mandatory.
* ACLP,ACTA, DDDLP or healthcare-cleaning experience will be an advantage.

Skills & Competencies
  
  

* Strong hands-on cleaning and operational knowledge.
* Good training, coaching and facilitation skills.
* Able to explain and demonstrate work processes clearly and practically.
* Able to guide both new hires and experienced supervisors.
* Patient and comfortable working with employees of different nationalities, languages and literacy levels.
* Strong observation and problem-solving skills.
* Able to identify capability gaps and provide immediate corrective coaching.
* Able to work independently across multiple sites.
* Good communication and interpersonal skills.
* Basic administrative skills for maintaining training and coaching records.
* Reliable, adaptable and responsive to changing operational requirements.

description:
**Entity:** Allianz Insurance Singapore
  
Allianz Insurance Singapore (AIS) has established itself as one of the fastest-growing General Insurance companies in the market, achieving remarkable success since its inception. **Description:**  
The HR Business Partner will partner with business leaders and employees while taking ownership of key HR operational activities, reporting into the Head of HR. This hands-on role is responsible for delivering effective HR services, supporting employee relations, ensuring operational compliance, providing people insights and reporting, and driving a positive employee experience.This is an exciting opportunity to join Allianz at a pivotal time, as AI reshapes the way we work. You will play a key role in shaping how our employees learn, transform and engage with the organisation, and have a real influence on how our HR processes are reimagined for the future. If you are passionate about combining people expertise with innovation to make a visible difference, this role offers the platform to do just that.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities:**  
a) HR Business Partnering Employee Relations
  
  

* Partner with managers and employees on day-to-day people matters across the employee lifecycle.
* Provide practical HR advice on performance management, employee relations, organisational changes, grievances, disciplinary matters and exits.
* Coach managers to manage people matters effectively, consistently and in line with company policies.

* Oversee day-to-day HR operations, including payroll, benefits administration, employee records and HR systems and processes.
* Manage onboarding formalities for new joiners, including enrollment into employee benefits.
* Ensure HR operational processes comply with company policies, internal controls and applicable Singapore employment requirements.
* Coordinate with internal teams, regional Centres of Excellence and external vendors to ensure accurate and timely delivery of HR services.

c) Reporting, Analytics Governance
  
  

* Prepare and deliver regular and ad-hoc HR reporting to internal and external stakeholders, including MOM reporting, CSRD people-related disclosures and quarterly HR metrics, ensuring accuracy, timeliness and appropriate governance.
* Maintain HR data integrity and provide meaningful people insights to the Head of HR and business leaders.
* Support internal and external audits and HR governance requirements.
* Track key HR metrics, identify trends and highlight operational risks or areas requiring attention.

d) Employee Engagement People Initiatives
  
  

* Support employee engagement, culture, wellbeing and inclusion initiatives.
* Analyse employee feedback and support leaders in developing and implementing appropriate actions.
* Drive the local implementation of relevant regional and Group People Culture programmes.
* Support HR projects, process improvements and transformation initiatives as required.
* Champion HR transformation by automating and streamlining processes and making effective use of available AI technology to elevate the HRBP role towards more strategic, insight-led business partnering.

**Qualifications and Skills:**  

* Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business, Psychology or a related discipline.
* 3+ years of progressive HR experience, ideally within HR business partnering or a broad HR generalist role.
* Strong working knowledge of HR operations, payroll, employee relations and Singapore employment practices.
* Ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities.
* Strong analytical skills with good proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Copilot, Agents, Power Automate
* Strong stakeholder management, communication and problem-solving skills.
* Experience in insurance, financial services or another regulated environment would be advantageous.
* Experience with SAP SuccessFactors would be an advantage.

title: Associate Director, Client Solutions
description:
About the role
  
  
As an Associate Director, Client Solutions, you will own operational excellence for a high-profile APAC client. You will lead the operations function across one or more client teams. You will be a senior partner to the Client Services Lead and a trusted advisor to client and agency leadership. You will set the operating model and delivery rhythm, and you will be accountable for delivery quality, risk, and efficiency. You will lead, coach, and develop a team of operations managers and associates. You will also help shape operational best practice across the wider business.
  
  
Reporting line
  
  
This role reports directly to the Senior Business Operations Director. It works in close partnership with the Client Services Lead and the wider client leadership team.
  
  
What you'll do
  
  
Leading delivery and client operations
  
  
Own end-to-end delivery for the client. Make sure scopes of work become robust, integrated plans that meet client expectations on time, on budget, and to quality standards.
  
  
Be accountable for delivery risk. Set up the governance, risk, and issue management approach, and drive resolution of the most complex challenges.
  
  
Set the operating rhythm for the client. This covers planning cycles, ceremonies, reporting cadence, and escalation paths. Make sure it is understood and followed across the cross-functional team.
  
  
Partner with Resource Management on capacity and demand planning. Make sure the right people and skills are in place now and for the future, and resolve resource challenges early.
  
  
Provide the Senior Business Operations Director and Client Services leadership with clear, insight-led reporting on performance, risk, and opportunity. Escalate with recommendations.
  
  
Act as a senior partner to Client Services on client and partner management by:
  
  
Preparing for and leading operational conversations with senior client and regional stakeholders.
  
  
Holding teams accountable for their deliverables and inputs.
  
  
Facilitating key client meetings, governance forums, and business reviews.
  
  
Making sure decisions, actions, and follow-ups are documented and tracked.
  
  
Work with Client Services on scope management and commercial discipline. This includes spotting scope changes, supporting change request conversations, and protecting delivery margin.
  
  
Anticipate issues before they arise. Put mitigation plans in place with Client Services and agency leadership.
  
  
Make sure the team understands the client's service level agreements. Hold the team to them, and own the approach for reporting against SLAs.
  
  
Model effective collaboration and communication, and champion it across the cross-functional team and with the client.
  
  
Driving operational effectiveness
  
  
Lead team wash-ups and retrospectives. Turn the findings into measurable improvements, and own their implementation.
  
  
Own the application of the end-to-end Campaign Delivery Process and Quality Standards across your client team. Track adherence and remove barriers to adoption.
  
  
Use data and performance metrics to identify trends, root causes, and efficiency opportunities. Make evidence-based recommendations to senior leadership.
  
  
Identify opportunities to improve productivity, tooling, automation, and ways of working. Lead their rollout across the client team.
  
  
Contribute to the wider operations community by shaping best practice, templates, and standards that can scale across teams and clients.
  
  
Leadership and talent development
  
  
Lead, coach, and develop a team of Operations Managers and Associates. This includes objective setting, performance feedback, and career development.
  
  
Build team capability through mentoring, structured onboarding, and knowledge sharing.
  
  
Act as the point of escalation and guidance for the team on complex or ambiguous delivery situations.
  
  
Support resourcing and hiring decisions for the operations team, and help build a strong succession pipeline.
  
  
Foster an inclusive, high-performing team culture built on accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
  
  
Key requirements
  
  
10+ years of relevant professional experience, ideally in a media agency and/or management consulting firm. This should include substantial experience leading delivery for large, complex, or multi-market clients.
  
  
Proven experience leading and developing teams, either through direct line management or by leading teams without formal authority.
  
  
Demonstrated track record of managing senior client relationships and influencing stakeholders across functions, regions, and levels, including senior leadership. Experience with APAC or multi-market stakeholders is a strong plus.
  
  
Experience owning delivery risk, governance, and quality for complex programmes. This includes working with scope, budgets, and commercial considerations.
  
  
Strong grounding in project and programme management methodologies, and a record of delivering complex, cross-functional work.
  
  
Experience working in Agile environments, including leading sprint planning, stand-ups, retrospectives, and other Scrum ceremonies.
  
  
Strong analytical and data-driven problem-solving skills, including root-cause analysis and translating insight into action.
  
  
A strategic, curious mindset about business operations. You identify opportunities and drive change that improves effectiveness and efficiency.
  
  
Sound judgement and the ability to make decisions and resolve issues in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment.
  
  
Excellent organisational skills and attention to detail. You bring structure and clarity to complex situations.
  
  
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present confidently to senior audiences.
  
  
Outstanding stakeholder management and relationship-building skills, with the credibility to influence and collaborate at all levels.
  
  
A proactive, adaptable mindset. You can manage multiple priorities and stay composed under pressure.
  
  
A positive attitude, high energy, and a collaborative approach to teamwork.
  
  
Life at WPP Media & Benefits
  
  
Our passion for shaping the next era of media includes investing in our employees to help them do their best work, and we’re just as committed to employee growth as we are to responsible media investment. WPP Media employees can tap into the global WPP Media & WPP networks to pursue their passions, grow their networks, and learn at the cutting edge of marketing and advertising. We have a variety of employee resource groups and host frequent in-office events showcasing team wins, sharing thought leadership, and celebrating holidays and milestone events. Our benefits include competitive medical, group retirement plans, vision, and dental insurance, significant paid time off, preferential partner discounts, and employee mental health awareness days.
  
  
WPP Media is an equal opportunity employer and considers applicants for all positions without discrimination or regard to particular characteristics. We are committed to fostering a culture of respect in which everyone feels they belong and has the same opportunities to progress in their careers.
  
  
We believe the best work happens when we're together, fostering creativity, collaboration, and connection. That's why we’ve adopted a hybrid approach, with teams in the office around four days a week. If you require accommodations or flexibility, please discuss this with the hiring team during the interview process.

title: Director, Expense Management
description:
You are as unique as your background, experience and point of view. Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered and challenged to be your best self. You'll work with dynamic colleagues - experts in their fields - who are eager to share their knowledge with you. Your leaders will inspire and help you reach your potential and soar to new heights. Every day, you'll have new and exciting opportunities to make life brighter for our Clients - who are at the heart of everything we do.

  

At Sun Life, we're driven by our Purpose: helping our Clients achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives. Our values shape how we work: caring, authentic, bold, inspiring, and impactful.

  

When you join Sun Life, you'll work with passionate colleagues and empowering leaders who support your growth and celebrate your contributions, so you can make a meaningful difference in our Clients' lives.

  

Discover how you can make a difference in the lives of individuals, families and communities around the world.

  
  

**Job Description:**

**Role Title:** Director, Expense Management

**Location:** Hong Kong or Singapore

**Company/Entity:** Sun Life Private Wealth

  

*At Sun Life, we’re driven by our Purpose: to help Clients build lifetime financial security and lead healthier lives. Across Sun Life Private Wealth, we cultivate a High-Performance, Caring Culture that empowers our people to achieve outstanding results, embrace continuous growth, and create meaningful impact. We succeed together by fostering an inclusive environment where wellbeing, collaboration, and accountability are equally valued.*

  

**What you will be doing**

Reporting to the Head of FP&A, Capital Management, and Reinsurance, the Director, Expense Management owns expense management for Sun Life Private Wealth and acts as a trusted business partner to function heads and senior leaders.

  

The role leads expense planning, budgeting, forecasting, and variance analysis for the business. Partnering with functional leaders, the Director challenges how the business spends and invests, driving expense efficiency, productivity, and measurable business value. Key business partners include Financial Planning & Analysis, Controller functions, Group Office, and Private Wealth leaders across Asia and North America.

  

**The role can be based in either Hong Kong or Singapore, and requires flexibility to work with colleagues across time zones, particularly during quarter-end and plan cycles.**

  

Accountabilities for the role include:

* *Business Partnership*

* *Act as the primary finance partner to Private Wealth function heads and cost-center owners, supporting their priorities while constructively challenging spending, resourcing, and vendor decisions*

* *Translate expense results, drivers, and trends into clear insights, practical options, and recommendations that support decisions by the CFO, CEO, and Leadership Team*

* *Provide expense and cost/benefit input to business cases and strategic initiatives, and track initiative spend and benefits realization against commitments*

* *Planning & Budgeting*

* *Own the expense planning and forecasting process, including the annual budget, annual expense study, strategic plan, and forecasts in partnership with FP&A*

* *Lead cost-center management, working with owners to set budgets, validate assumptions (eg. headcount, travel, and initiative spend) and hold them accountable to plan*

* *Lead monthly and quarterly variance analysis against plan and prior forecasts, providing commentary for management reporting and flagging emerging risks and opportunities*

* *Develop and maintain methodologies to allocate shared service expenses among operating entities, including ongoing reporting and analytics*

* *Productivity & Optimization*

* *Identify and drive expense optimization opportunities across Private Wealth*

* *Set and track productivity targets with cost-center owners*

* *Leadership & Collaboration*

* *Lead a team of two direct reports, setting priorities and building team capabilities*

* *Partner with the Controller function to ensure a clear handoff between expense management (plans, forecasts, and analysis) and expense accounting (actuals, accruals, and close), coordinating reporting requirements with the Group Office and other Finance teams*

* *Continuously improve expense processes, tools and reporting*

* *Provide ad hoc project support across the CFO and Strategy functions*

  

***What we are looking for***

* *Minimum of 10 years of relevant experience in expense management, financial reporting, or a related finance discipline, ideally within insurance or financial services, including team leadership experience*

* *A professional designation (eg. CPA, CFA, or FSA) or equivalent experience is an asset*

* *Strong knowledge of budgeting, forecasting, cost management, and expense allocation*

* *A strategic mindset combined with hands-on experience using financial systems and reporting tools (eg. general ledger systems, Hyperion, Excel, Alteryx)*

* *Clear communication skills, translating complex financial information into actionable recommendations*

* *Strong stakeholder management skills, building trust with senior leaders across functions while challenging spending without formal authority*

* *Proven ability to maintain financial discipline and control across budgets, forecasts, costs, and benefits realization*

* *Ability to anticipate emerging risks and help the business take action early*

* *Demonstrated people leadership skills with the ability to coach team members, take ownership of delivery and manage multiple priorities*

  

*We encourage you to explore our Private Wealth page to learn more about our business, solutions, and latest developments:* https://www.linkedin.com/company/sun-life-private-wealth/

Finance

28/01/2027

title: Assistant Director
description:
COMPANY DESCRIPTION
  
  
Montfort Care is a social service agency that works with individuals, families and communities to create new possibilities. Founded in 2000, we now employ more than 400 employees and operate from over 30 locations in Singapore across Anti-Violence, Family Service, Mental Health, Caregiving and Eldercare services.
  
  
Guided by our founding ethos, "Those whom the world rejects must move you the most", we believe no life should be defined by its hardest circumstances. Behind every struggle is a person or family with dignity, strengths and possibilities yet to be realised. Our work begins by seeing what others may overlook and creating the conditions for people to reclaim agency, rebuild relationships and shape a different future.
  
  
Find out more at www.montfortcare.org.sg
  
  
RESPONSIBILITIES
  
  
The Strategy & Growth team is an organisation-wide capability-building function for Montfort Care (MFC), partnering with leaders and teams to address the organisation's most complex and pressing challenges. It combines strategic thinking, transformation expertise and implementation to strengthen organisational capabilities and achieve sustainable impact.
  
  
The
  
  
Assistant Director
  
  
, Transformation leads organisation-wide transformation initiatives that improve service effectiveness, operational efficiency and client experience. Reporting to the Director, Strategy & Growth, the role has a strong focus on rethinking service delivery through digital means while ensuring that services remain accessible and inclusive for clients who may face barriers to digital adoption. The portfolio also includes non-digital aspects that enable digital service delivery, including service redesign, process improvement, operating model changes and new ways of working.
  
  
Working closely with the Director, Strategy & Growth, leadership, service leaders and corporate service functions, the Assistant Director identifies high-value digital transformation opportunities and leads initiatives from discovery and business case development through experimentation, implementation, adoption and benefits realisation. The role applies user-centred, agile and data-informed approaches to translate organisational and client needs into scalable solutions.
  
  
The
  
  
Assistant Director
  
  
, Transformation develops the internal capabilities required to sustain new ways of working. The role champions responsible experimentation, digital confidence and continuous improvement, ensuring that transformation strengthens outcomes for clients and employees without leaving digitally less-confident users behind.
  
  
This is a high-visibility role with frequent opportunities to engage and present to the Chief Executive Officer and leadership team. The
  
  
Assistant Director
  
  
must understand strategic intent, exercise sound judgement and translate broad direction into coherent priorities, practical action plans and measurable outcomes. The role offers an opportunity for a transformation practitioner to step into a wider organisational remit and make a significant contribution to Montfort Care's service and organisational outcomes.
  
  
Organisation Strategy Alignment and Transformation Planning
  
  
Partner with leadership, service leaders, employees and clients to define the future of social service delivery and identify the operating models, capabilities and transformation priorities required to realise it.
  
  
Define measurable outcomes and benefits for transformation initiatives, including improvements in client experience, service effectiveness, employee productivity, adoption, accessibility, efficiency and cost, and establish mechanisms to track benefits from baseline through implementation and scale-up.
  
  
Lead research, horizon scanning and analysis of client needs, sector developments, emerging technologies and new service delivery models. Translate findings into clear opportunity statements and evidence-based recommendations for leadership consideration.
  
  
Work with leadership to shape and prioritise a portfolio of digital and non-digital transformation initiatives based on strategic relevance, client and employee value, feasibility, inclusion, risk, resource requirements and expected benefits.
  
  
Facilitating annual/ multi-year strategic planning cycles. Lead secretariat function to organize MFC's annual work plan; this includes pre-retreat planning, conduct of retreats, and organising of cascade briefs to middle managers and front liners.
  
  
Transformation Project Management
  
  
Map out and track transformation project progress against MFC's strategic objectives to ensure alignment of transformation projects to broader organisational goals.
  
  
Establish governance structure for identified transformation projects based on organisation priorities; e.g. project organisation, project charter, timelines, resources, and accountability.
  
  
Engage stakeholders to build understanding of transformation objectives and drive ownership of transformation objectives by service pillars.
  
  
Diagnose broad or ambiguous symptoms, frame clear problem statements and identify root causes through data analysis, user research and process mapping. Conceptualise and implement fit-for-purpose responses, which may include service redesign, digital solutions, process improvement, operating model or organisation structure changes, capability development, and leadership or culture interventions.
  
  
Coach and guide Transformation team and Service Pillar Heads on transformation frameworks, methodologies, change management approaches and best practices. Support leadership in resolving organisation-wide structural, operational, or cultural barriers to transformation success.
  
  
Together with Service Pillar Heads, Transformation team, Communications team, drive change management strategies to enable success of transformation projects.
  
  
Track and manage transformation project progress and risks to ensure timely delivery of transformation milestones.
  
  
Design and deliver a tiered digital capability programme that can be scaled across more than 400 employees, covering foundational digital literacy, role-specific skills and advanced capabilities for digital champions. Develop playbooks, communities of practice, coaching and practical learning interventions that build a digital-first culture while supporting employees with different levels of confidence and readiness.
  
  
Experimentation and scaling
  
  
Lead research, experimentation and pilots for new ways of delivering services. Define hypotheses and success measures, test solutions with employees and clients, evaluate evidence and risks, and recommend whether initiatives should be stopped, refined or scaled.
  
  
Vendor Management
  
  
Build and manage partnerships with technology providers, social service agencies, public-sector bodies, research institutions and other ecosystem partners or vendors to co-develop and deliver transformation initiatives. Establish clear outcomes, governance, responsibilities and performance measures for joint projects.
  
  
Manage and track KPIs of vendors to ensure service delivered meet our contractual needs.
  
  
Funding Management
  
  
Research relevant grants and funding opportunities, and develop use cases and applications that support digital and broader transformation initiatives. Manage funding commitments, budgets, milestones, reporting and benefit measures to ensure compliance and intended outcomes.
  
  
Plan yearly departmental budget and be accountable for the expenditure of these funds in support of MFC organisational objectives.
  
  
People Management
  
  
Lead and develop strategy and transformation teams to drive delivery of organisational objectives.
  
  
Foster a culture of innovation in the team to meet social mission and objectives.
  
  
Risk and Compliance
  
  
Understand IPC (Institute of Public Character) and charity organisations compliance and regulatory requirements and ensure adherence.
  
  
Identify and manage transformation risks, including data protection, cybersecurity, accessibility, ethical use of technology, vendor dependency, service continuity and unintended exclusion of clients. Work with relevant corporate service functions and funders to ensure that initiatives meet applicable regulatory, security and governance requirements.
  
  
Others
  
  
Responsibilities listed above are not exhaustive. From time to time, additional duties or projects may be assigned based on organisational needs.
  
  
QUALIFICATIONS
  
  
Bachelor's degree from a recognised institution of higher learning in business, information technology, information systems, engineering, social sciences, public policy, organisational development or a related discipline. An advanced degree in business administration, information technology or a related field is advantageous.
  
  
Project Management Professional (PMP) certification, Change management certifications (e.g. Prosci) is advantageous but not mandatory.
  
  
OTHER INFORMATION
  
  
Relevant Experience and Required Competencies
  
  
At least 7-10 years of progressive experience in management consulting, internal transformation, service design, digital transformation, innovation or major programme delivery, including demonstrated experience leading digital initiatives from problem definition through implementation and adoption.
  
  
Prior experience in a major technology company, digital consultancy or technology-enabled organisation, with responsibility for delivering digital products or initiatives for internal or external users.
  
  
Experience in social sector, healthcare, or mission-driven organisations is advantageous. Candidates from other sectors with an interest in driving the change in the social service sector are encouraged to apply.
  
  
3-5 years of leading teams or major workstreams with a demonstrated ability to drive organisation-wide strategy and transformation projects. Hands-on experience in driving transformation planning, stakeholder engagement and governance.
  
  
Experience working with data, KPI, OKRs, dashboarding for reporting for leadership teams.
  
  
Experience in driving process redesign, operating model/ organisation structure, skilling strategy, leadership and culture initiatives.
  
  
Demonstrated ability to navigate complex, multi-stakeholder initiatives, establish priorities based on organisational needs and delivery capacity, and build alignment across service, corporate and technology stakeholders.
  
  
Ability to lead concurrent initiatives using an agile, test-and-learn mindset while maintaining disciplined governance over scope, priorities, interdependencies, resources, risks and delivery commitments. The candidate must be able to adapt the approach when evidence or organisational needs change without allowing uncontrolled scope expansion.
  
  
Strong analytical ability & problem-solving skills to identify critical areas for action in a data-informed manner.
  
  
Executive presence and sound judgement to engage senior leadership, challenge assumptions constructively and influence decisions, combined with the ability to explain complex transformation and digital concepts to frontline employees and non-technical stakeholders to build understanding and commitment.
  
  

* Only shortlisted candidates will be notified.

Please note that your application will be sent to and reviewed by the direct employer - Montfort Care

title: Director of Growth
description:
UPGroup Asia | Singapore & Southeast Asia
  
  
The Role
  
  
We are seeking an entrepreneurial and commercially driven Director of Growth to lead UPGroup Asia's next phase of expansion.
  
  
Reporting to the Group CEO, this role will be responsible for developing and executing a 3–5 year growth strategy that accelerates revenue, strengthens profitability and expands the Group's presence across Southeast Asia.
  
  
Beyond traditional business development, the Director of Growth will identify new markets, strategic partnerships, business channels and revenue streams, including opportunities to develop proprietary intellectual property (IP) and scalable business models.
  
  
The successful candidate will play a pivotal role in achieving measurable year-on-year revenue growth while maintaining a healthy EBITDA margin annually, building a sustainable and profitable regional business.
  
  
Key Responsibilities
  
  
1. Drive Group Revenue & EBITDA Growth
  
  
Develop and execute a 3–5 year growth strategy aligned with the Group's long-term business objectives.
  
  
Drive agreed year-on-year revenue growth while maintaining the agreed EBITDA margin.
  
  
Identify and prioritise high-growth opportunities across Events, AV Production, Venue Management and other complementary businesses.
  
  
Work closely with business unit leaders to improve profitability, optimise commercial performance and accelerate sustainable growth.
  
  
2. Develop New Business Channels & Revenue Streams
  
  
Identify, develop and launch new business channels, products and revenue streams that complement the Group's existing capabilities.
  
  
Explore opportunities to develop proprietary IP, owned events, experiential concepts and recurring revenue models.
  
  
Evaluate new business opportunities based on market potential, scalability, profitability and long-term commercial value.
  
  
Build business cases, go-to-market strategies and execution plans to successfully commercialise new initiatives.
  
  
3. Expand Regional Markets & Strategic Partnerships
  
  
Identify and develop growth opportunities across Singapore and key Southeast Asian markets.
  
  
Establish strategic partnerships with venue owners, hotel groups, convention centres, agencies, brands and corporate clients.
  
  
Develop market-entry strategies and commercial partnerships that enable scalable regional expansion.
  
  
Secure long-term commercial agreements and strategic alliances that generate sustainable revenue.
  
  
4. Lead Strategic Commercial Growth
  
  
Identify and secure high-value business opportunities, strategic accounts and multi-year commercial agreements.
  
  
Develop cross-selling opportunities that leverage the Group's integrated Events, AV, Creative and Venue Management capabilities.
  
  
Work alongside business development and account management teams to strengthen client relationships, increase account value and unlock new opportunities.
  
  
Establish commercially sound pricing, negotiation and partnership frameworks that protect profitability.
  
  
5. Strengthen Growth Execution & Commercial Performance
  
  
Translate strategic growth initiatives into measurable annual business plans, financial targets and execution milestones.
  
  
Establish clear reporting on revenue growth, EBITDA performance, new business channels and regional expansion.
  
  
Collaborate with business unit leaders to ensure growth strategies are operationally achievable and commercially sustainable.
  
  
Drive a culture of commercial accountability, innovation and disciplined execution across the Group.
  
  
What You Bring
  
  
10–15+ years of experience in commercial leadership, business development, corporate strategy or regional growth, preferably within Events, Experiential Marketing, Media, Hospitality or related industries.
  
  
Experience in a senior leadership role within an established regional organisation, with demonstrated involvement in scaling its business.
  
  
A proven track record of delivering double-digit revenue growth while maintaining or improving profitability.
  
  
Experience developing new business channels, commercialising new products, proprietary IP or recurring revenue streams.
  
  
Strong commercial and financial acumen, including P&L management, gross margins, EBITDA and business planning.
  
  
Experience developing and executing multi-year growth strategies across multiple business units or Southeast Asian markets.
  
  
Established senior-level industry relationships and the ability to negotiate complex strategic partnerships and commercial agreements.
  
  
An entrepreneurial mindset with the ability to identify opportunities, build business cases and translate strategies into measurable commercial results.
  
  
Strong leadership, stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to influence cross-functional teams and senior executives.
  
  
How Success Will Be Measured
  
  
1. Revenue Growth
  
  
Achieve agreed year-on-year revenue growth through new business opportunities, strategic partnerships, regional expansion and new revenue streams.
  
  
2. EBITDA Performance
  
  
Maintain the agreed annual EBITDA margin, ensuring growth initiatives contribute positively to the Group's overall profitability.
  
  
3. New Business Channels & Revenue Streams
  
  
Successfully develop and commercialise new business channels, proprietary IP, products or recurring revenue models that generate measurable financial contributions.
  
  
4. Regional Expansion
  
  
Establish and scale commercially viable operations and strategic partnerships across priority Southeast Asian markets.
  
  
5. Strategic Partnerships & Commercial Growth
  
  
Secure meaningful multi-year commercial agreements, strategic accounts and partnerships that strengthen the Group's competitive position and long-term revenue visibility.
  
  
6. Strategy Execution & Leadership
  
  
Develop and execute a clear 3–5 year growth roadmap, supported by measurable annual milestones, financial accountability and effective collaboration across business units.

title: Business Development Director
description:
Reporting to the President, Medical Marketing Strategic Unit, the SEA Business Development Director is a senior regional commercial leadership role focused on accelerating growth with pharmaceutical and healthcare clients across South-East Asia. This is a high-impact opportunity for a proven business developer to shape regional client partnerships, unlock cross-market opportunities, and position MIMS as a strategic medical marketing and communications partner.
  
  
The role directly leads business development and account success teams, while working closely with SEA country business directors to grow priority regional accounts. The successful candidate will bring strong pharmaceutical client relationships, consultative selling capability, and the credibility to influence senior stakeholders internally and externally.
  
  
**Key responsibilities of this position include:**  
Lead regional and cluster based business development strategy and engagement among pharmaceutical and healthcare clients, securing new business, expanding existing relationships, and delivering revenue and profitability targets across SEA.
  
  
Lead strategic account planning for priority clients, identifying growth opportunities across markets, therapy areas, brands, and service lines.
  
  
Build trusted senior client relationships and use sector credibility to open doors, shape opportunities, and strengthen MIMS’ position as a regional partner.
  
  
Lead, coach, and align business development and account success teams to deliver consultative sales excellence, disciplined account growth, and strong client servicing.
  
  
Coordinate with SEA country business directors to align account strategies, identify cross-market opportunities, and ensure consistent regional client engagement.
  
  
Develop compelling multi-channel medical communications and marketing solutions with internal strategy, medical, editorial, creative, digital, operations, and platform teams.
  
  
Lead RFI, RFP, proposal, and pitch processes, including solution design, commercial strategy, budgeting, procurement negotiation, and profitability management.
  
  
Support MSAs, preferred supplier arrangements, and other commercial frameworks with key clients where appropriate.
  
  
Source and share market intelligence, client insights, and best practices across SEA teams to improve win rates, account growth, and regional commercial capability.
  
  
Contribute as a senior member of the regional leadership team, helping shape commercial strategy and raise the profile of MIMS products and services.
  
  
**Key Requirements:**  
Senior business development, sales, commercial leadership, or key account management experience, ideally in medical communications, healthcare marketing, pharmaceutical services, medical education, or a comparable B2B service environment.
  
  
Proven success personally winning new business, growing strategic accounts, and delivering revenue targets with regional pharmaceutical MNC clients.
  
  
Established senior client network across pharmaceutical, healthcare, or related sectors in Singapore and South East Asia.
  
  
Strong understanding of medical communications, medical education, healthcare marketing, or similar solutions, with the ability to convert client needs into commercially viable proposals.
  
  
Experience leading business development, account management, account success, or client servicing teams to deliver sales growth and high-quality client outcomes.
  
  
Ability to influence across a matrix regional structure and collaborate effectively with country leaders and cross-functional delivery teams.
  
  
Commercially sharp and financially literate, with confidence in pricing, budgets, procurement discussions, profitability, and forecasting.
  
  
Excellent communication, presentation, negotiation, and senior stakeholder management skills.
  
  
Highly driven, resilient, organised, and comfortable operating independently while bringing teams together around shared regional opportunities.
  
  
University degree preferred; scientific, healthcare, business, or marketing qualifications advantageous.
  
  
MIMS PTE. LTD.
  
  
MIMS is a leading healthcare media company providing tailored solutions to a global healthcare market. We provide reference data, decision support solutions, news and education to communities of general practitioners, specialist doctors, pharmacists, nurses and patients across 13 countries.
  
  
We produce a range of professional media including data-rich directories, electronic and online products, journals and face-to-face meetings. The established and trusted reputation of our brands means that many of them are embedded in the daily workflow of the healthcare communities they serve.
  
  
Serving healthcare professionals in Asia for nearly 40 years, MIMS is focused on providing tools to meet physicians' needs in their daily practice, as well as committing to support lifelong learning needs of healthcare professionals and consumers.
  
  
MIMS Drug Information System is the most advanced, complete, and up-to-date information source on available products, delivering critical information needed at every point of care. MIMS Drug Information System is delivered across multiple platforms and channels, available in print, online and LAN, standalone or integrated.
  
  
In the area of Continuing Medical Education, MIMS has developed a diverse platform of educational products and services in the form of live events, enduring materials in print, e-media and web.

title: Deputy Director
description:
Role Overview
  
  
The Deputy Director is a key leadership role responsible for overseeing program delivery, strengthening operational systems, and supporting organizational sustainability.
  
  
This role ensures high-quality, trauma-informed service delivery while also strengthening Casa Raudha’s ability to translate programme outcomes into clear impact narratives that support funding, partnerships, and long-term sustainability.
  
  
The role requires strong leadership in operations, people management, and systems building, with the ability to connect frontline services to strategic and organizational outcomes.
  
  
Key Responsibilities
  
  
1. Program Leadership & Service Delivery
  
  
Oversee shelter services, including crisis, the independent (Dahlia@Casa Raudha and the programmes
  
  
Ensure consistent delivery of trauma-informed, survivor-centred care
  
  
Strengthen case management, safety planning, and discharge readiness processes
  
  
Monitor and improve client outcomes, including safety, stability, and independence
  
  
Ensure quality and consistency of service delivery frameworks
  
  
2. Operations & Systems Management
  
  
Develop, review, and strengthen SOPs, safeguarding, and operational protocols
  
  
Ensure compliance with relevant regulatory and funding requirements
  
  
Build and improve internal systems (case tracking, reporting tools, dashboards)
  
  
Oversee operational readiness, safety standards, and resource management
  
  
3. Team Leadership & Capability Building
  
  
Supervise and support programme and operations staff
  
  
Build a culture of accountability, collaboration, and professional practice
  
  
Implement staff training in areas such as crisis intervention and trauma-informed care
  
  
Support staff wellbeing and contribute to workload and burnout management strategies
  
  
4. Partnerships & External Engagement
  
  
Support the Executive Director in managing partnerships with government agencies, community organizations, and corporates
  
  
Develop and maintain working relationships with relevant stakeholders in the social service ecosystem
  
  
Represent the organization in selected external engagements when required
  
  
Identify collaboration opportunities that enhance service delivery and organizational outcomes
  
  
5. Fundraising Support & ImpactCommunication
  
  
Support development of grant proposals, donor reports, and funding submissions
  
  
Translate programme outcomes and data into clear, compelling impact narratives
  
  
Work with leadership to strengthen donor communication and stewardship materials
  
  
Contribute programme insights to fundraising strategy and partnership development
  
  
Support identification of funding opportunities aligned with organizational needs
  
  
6. Strategy & Organizational Development
  
  
Support execution of organizational strategic priorities
  
  
Translate strategy into operational plans and measurable deliverables
  
  
Identify service gaps and contribute to programme improvement and innovation
  
  
Provide programme-level input to organizational planning and development
  
  
7. Monitoring, Evaluation & Reporting
  
  
Develop and track key performance indicators (KPIs) across programmes
  
  
Analyze service data and identify trends to support decision-making
  
  
Strengthen outcome measurement frameworks (e.g. safety, stability, independence)
  
  
Prepare reports for internal leadership, Board, and external stakeholders
  
  
Support improvement of data quality and impact reporting systems
  
  
Requirements
  
  
Qualifications & Experience
  
  
Degree in Social Work, Psychology, or related discipline (Postgraduate qualification an advantage)
  
  
Minimum 8–10 years of relevant experience in social services or related fields
  
  
At least 3–5 years of leadership or supervisory experience
  
  
Experience in crisis intervention, shelter services, or domestic violence work is preferred
  
  
Core Competencies
  
  
Strong leadership and people management capability
  
  
Experience in building or improving operational systems and processes
  
  
Ability to translate programme work into reports, proposals, and impact narratives
  
  
Strong stakeholder and partnership management skills
  
  
Analytical and data-informed decision-making ability
  
  
Knowledge of trauma-informed and person-centred approaches
  
  
Ability to work effectively in complex and high-pressure environments
  
  
Key Attributes
  
  
Grounded, stable, and emotionally intelligent leadership style
  
  
Able to balance care, accountability, and operational discipline
  
  
Strong alignment with social service values and client-centred practice
  
  
Resilient, adaptable, and able to work in fast-evolving environments
  
  
Strong communication and influencing skills
  
  
Casa Raudha Ltd is a dedicated social service organization focused on supporting survivors of domestic violence. Initially established to provide shelter for those in crisis, Casa Raudha has since broadened its services to include community outreach, awareness programs, and initiatives aimed at fostering family resilience. The organization is committed to building a society free from domestic violence by helping families stay united in a healthy and conducive home environment.

description:

req39500

12/1/2026 (MM/DD/YYYY) at 11:59pm UTC

**Description**

At the International Finance Corporation (IFC), a member of the World Bank Group (WBG), you’ll join a diverse, global community working across cultures, disciplines, and borders to address the world’s most pressing development challenges. With 1.2 billion young people reaching working age in the decade ahead, the challenge of job creation has never been greater. Through partnerships across 145 countries and more than 182 offices worldwide, we work with governments, private sector, development partners and other stakeholders to invest in people, strengthen markets, and deliver scalable, data-driven solutions that generate more and better jobs and improve lives. In fiscal year 2026, IFC committed a record $105.6 billion to private companies and financial institutions in developing countries. For more information, visit www.ifc.org.  
  
IFC is seeking a Country Advisory and Economics Manager for the Asia and Pacific/East Asia and Pacific region. The Manager will lead a team of economics, strategy, and operational staff responsible for:  
1. Producing both regional and country-level economic assessments to support IFC’s strategy and operations;  
2. Collaborating with regional and industry colleagues to produce analytical products such as Country Private Sector Diagnostics (CPSDs) and IFC Country Strategies;  
3. Significantly contributing to WBG products such as Systematic Country Diagnostics (SCD), Country Climate and Development Reports (CCDR), and IBRD/IDA lending operations; and  
4. Putting IFC’s country strategy and diagnostic recommendations into practice through Advisory projects that engage with governments, regulators, civil society, development partners and other relevant stakeholders to reform markets and sectors and address key bottlenecks to private sector development.  
  
The Manager will be a motivated and dynamic professional, with excellent analytical skills and relevant policy and industry experience. S/he will have expertise in private sector development, applied research, and analytical products with an extensive history of hands-on interaction with government clients and public sector stakeholders.

The Manager will be based in Singapore, reporting to the Division Directors, and will be a member of the Asia Regional Management Team. The role will entail close collaboration with units across the Asia region, as well as with global industry departments, the Economics and Private Sector Development Vice-Presidency, IBRD/IDA, MIGA, and external organizations.  
  
**Duties and accountabilities:**  
  
Strategic and Economic Analysis  

* Support the Regional Management Team in formulating country and regional strategies to maximize IFC's impact and address development challenges.
* Support Regional Directors and Country Mangers in WBG processes such as Systematic Country Diagnostics and Country Partnership Frameworks, in close cooperation with the relevant industry and IBRD/IDA and MIGA teams.
* Coordinate the production of new Country Strategies and Business Plans to establish a strategic direction for IFC’s program at the country level.
* Liaise with IBRD/IDA and IMF to leverage their knowledge and support in delivering IFC’s work program.
* Inform Regional Management Team and IFC Senior Management on major risks to the IFC program and portfolio in the region based on economic analysis and information gathered.
* Lead the team of regional economists as they produce/contribute to analytical reports and policy notes on main economic issues pertaining to the region—at the macro level and sectoral level, including but not limited to the Country Private Sector Diagnostics and Country Climate and Development Reports.

  
Operational Delivery  

* Lead the team to operationalize key strategic and diagnostic recommendations through the design and implementation of government-facing Advisory Services projects that support reform implementation and investment facilitation in line with IFC’s strategic priorities.
* Ensure a high quality of the unit’s operations through a focus on project design (development results, project reviews, lessons learned) throughout an individual project cycle and across the unit’s portfolio of operations, with a focus on achieving high development effectiveness.
* Ensure proactive monitoring of the operational portfolio’s funding needs, which includes engagement with regional partnership team; engage with development partners on performance/challenges; ensure quality donor reporting that meets donor expectations.

  
Operational Support  

* Engage throughout the project cycle to support other operational teams in developing their projects by providing advice on macro-economic trends, country and regional context and risks.
* Work closely with the Knowledge Bank Economics and Private Sector Vice Presidency as well as IBRD/IDA to coordinate advice to teams on development impact, creating markets and working within the World Bank Group to maximize the Cascade approach (i.e., working with governments and IBRD/IDA to first seek private sector solutions to address development challenges and reserve public financing for projects only when other options are suboptimal).
* Work closely with IBRD/IDA country economists and contribute to the design of lending operations.
* Support teams at Board meetings and meetings with Executive Directors to provide advice on country and regional context and strategic fit.

  
Managerial Responsibilities  

* Lead and manage the unit and ensure the team is high-performing, well-motivated and committed to the advancement of IFC’s strategic goals.
* Mentor and develop staff and promote opportunities for rotation and continued learning.
* Be part of, and actively contribute to Regional Management Team.
* Staff projects with the appropriate resources to deploy the most appropriate technical expertise and provide exceptional client service, while keeping in mind career and training development needs of staff.
* Manage, oversee, and optimize IFC’s internal and external funding mix and budget to efficiently deliver operations in the region, including through engagement in budgetary discussions and processes with regional, global and partnership teams.

**Selection Criteria**

* PhD or Masters in economics or related field and at least 12 years of experience in economics, economic development, private sector development, or related fields.
* Strong grounding in economics from academic and/or practical experience.
* Deep familiarity/experience in IFC, IDA/IBRD, MIGA or other financial institutions focused on the private sector, especially in developing countries.
* Extensive hands-on experience of working with government clients and public sector stakeholders, including regulators.
* Demonstrated ability to influence the policy dialogue and lead the development agenda at the country or regional level.
* Familiarity with the WBG operational products and instruments; first-hand experience of having worked on joint projects with IBRD/IDA will be an advantage.
* Ability to engage and collaborate closely with IBRD/IDA and IMF on policy and economic issues pertaining to the countries in the regions.
* Strong analytical, strategy formulation, and conceptual abilities.
* Demonstrated ability to think strategically, develop innovative solutions, challenge the status quo and make sound decisions to build IFC business.
* Ability to communicate clearly and concisely, both orally and in writing, as well as cultivate an active network of relationships inside and outside the organization and to represent IFC publicly as needed.
* Demonstrated interpersonal skills, proven ability to work effectively as a team leader, build high performing teams and manage and recruit talent.
* Ability to manage competing and sometimes unanticipated priorities, and tight deadlines.
* World Bank Group-wide managerial selection criteria including courage of your convictions, leading the team for impact, influencing across boundaries, fostering openness to new ideas, building talent for the future.

Additional Considerations  
  
As the World Bank Group continues to evolve, we value candidates who:  

* Demonstrate the ability to collaborate effectively across teams, disciplines, cultures, and institutional boundaries.
* Responsibly leverage digital and AI-enabled tools to enhance productivity, learning, and decision-making.
* Bring experience working on fragile, conflict-affected, and violent (FCV)-related contexts and are encouraged to highlight relevant experience in their application materials, where applicable.

**WBG Culture Attributes:**

1. Sense of urgency: Anticipate and quickly respond to the needs of internal and external stakeholders.  
2. Thoughtful risk-taking: Challenge the status quo and push boundaries to achieve greater impact.
  
3. Empowerment and accountability: Empower yourself and others to act and hold each other accountable for results.
